entries.content: read design/feature_descriptions/B_350_deleting_a_card_jumps_the_scrollbar_back_to_start.md. investigate what is happening, report your findings. Propose solution. Be short and to the point, full sentences.
I’ll trace the documented symptom through the card deletion, selection, and scrolling code paths. I’ll only report findings and a proposed solution; I won’t edit files.

---
author: 
id: B_350
internalId: ab825e36-710b-4c16-bd2c-59dad2825fb4
title: deleting a card jumps the scrollbar back to start
status: design
owner: 
affects:
agents:
  - design/activity/card__ab825e36-710b-4c16-bd2c-59dad2825fb4.json
policy:
---

When a column is long and we scrolled down to a card and delete that card again, it seems we do a full re-render of the card view instead of only the column that changed.

This alone should already prevent the bad scroll behavior.

The feature description’s “full re-render” diagnosis is not supported by the current code.

- Deletion rebuilds the project snapshot in [project_state.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_state.ts:280), then emits granular card lifecycle events.
- [use_card_column_cards.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/card_view/use_card_column_cards.ts:23) updates only the affected column.
- Cards and columns have stable keys, so the board’s scroll container in [card_view.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/card_view/card_view.tsx:248) is not remounted.
- The likely cause is browser scroll or focus restoration when the confirmation dialog and its owning card disappear. No code explicitly preserves the board scroll position.

Proposed solution: store the board container’s `scrollTop` and `scrollLeft` before deletion and restore them after the removal is rendered. Also prevent the delete dialog from restoring focus to the removed card. Add a real-browser regression test because jsdom cannot validate scrolling behavior.
if it is a focusing issue, can't we move the focus to the card before or after? would that solve the issue?

Yes, if focus restoration is the cause.

Do not focus the card being deleted because it immediately disappears. Before deletion, identify the next card, or the previous card when deleting the last one. After deletion, focus that card using:

```ts
element.focus({ preventScroll: true });
```

The delete dialog should also disable its automatic focus restoration; otherwise it may race with the explicit focus and target the removed card. If the scrollbar still resets after this change, focus was not the cause and the scroll position must be preserved explicitly.

Add `Current state`, `implementation details`, `acceptance criteria` for `design/feature_descriptions/B_350_deleting_a_card_jumps_the_scrollbar_back_to_start.md`.
update the field `status` in the markdown feature description file to `ready for implementation`.

**Title:** Error: Local Git project validation failed for "C:\Users\janbo\Documents\marketing\vidsy": Command failed: git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree

### Application stack frames

- `/C:/Users/janbo/AppData/Local/Programs/desktop/resources/app.asar/desktop/renderer/assets/index-D90FAwtc.js:136:2271` â€” vre

## Current state

The local project picker and the typed, recent, and startup local-project flows validate a folder through `resolveLocalProject`. It runs `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` and treats every failure as an unexpected error. `ProjectOpenFlowService` then passes that error to `dialogService.error`, which displays it and reports it to Sentry.

The reported folder was not a Git repository when it was selected. Its `.git` directory was created about two minutes after the Sentry event. This is a recoverable user choice, but the application currently offers no way to initialize the folder and continue. The Git process wrapper also discards `stderr` on unsuccessful commands, preventing reliable classification of the failure.

## Implementation details

- Preserve `stdout` and `stderr` on errors returned by `GitProcess`. This enriches failures for all desktop Git callers without changing their success or failure behavior.
- Add a shared, bridge-safe error code for a selected folder that is not a Git repository. Include the selected root path in the serialized error fields. Classify only Git's known â€œnot a git repositoryâ€ response this way; permission, executable, timeout, ownership, and other Git failures remain unexpected errors.
- Add a desktop bridge operation that initializes the selected folder with `git init`, using the folder as the process working directory and without constructing a shell command. Resolve the resulting local project through the existing validation path.
- Add a Git-initialization confirmation state to `ProjectOpenFlowService`. Use it for picker, typed, recent, and startup local-folder validation. Keep the selected path in the service while confirmation is open.
- Render the confirmation in the project-open dialog with the selected path and explicit Yes and No actions. If the user selects Yes, initialize the repository and continue the existing project-open flow. If the user selects No, clear the confirmation and return to local project selection without opening the project, showing another error, or reporting to Sentry.
- Report initialization failures and every other unexpected validation failure through `dialogService.error`. Do not report the expected not-a-repository result through Sentry.
- Add focused tests for failed Git output preservation, error classification and bridge transport, repository initialization, all local-project entry paths, confirmation actions, and expected versus unexpected telemetry routing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Selecting or entering a folder that is not a Git repository asks whether to create a local Git repository in that folder.
- Selecting Yes runs `git init`, validates the new repository, and continues opening the project through the existing flow.
- Selecting No does not initialize or open the project, does not show another error, and does not report the choice to Sentry.
- Picker, typed, recent, and startup local-folder flows use the same confirmation behavior.
- An existing Git repository opens without an initialization prompt and retains its current behavior.
- A failed `git init` does not open the project, shows the actionable Git failure, and is reported to Sentry.

  - app/src/services/application_startup_service.ts
---

## Current state

When the last project uses remote storage, startup creates a `RemoteControlStorageService` and attempts to restore the WebSocket connection before opening the project. If the remote desktop is unavailable, the connection rejects with `RemoteControlConnectionError: Remote-control connection failed`.

`ApplicationStartupService` treats this expected connectivity failure like any other project restoration failure. `App` then passes the composed restore message to `dialogService.error`, which reports it to Sentry. Because the reported value is a string rather than the original error, the event has no application stack frames.

`RemoteConnectionService` already owns remote connection status and its user-visible error. `RemoteConnectButton` also attempts the same-origin connection when it mounts and opens its connection dialog when that attempt fails. The generic restore dialog and Sentry event therefore duplicate the remote connection flow.

## Implementation details

- In `ApplicationStartupService`, treat `RemoteControlConnectionError` from initial project restoration as a recoverable startup outcome. Continue startup with no restored project resolution instead of setting `bootstrap.error`.
- Continue the remaining startup work, including the startup model-catalog refresh, after a recoverable remote connection failure.
- Keep the error in `RemoteConnectionService`, which already publishes the disconnected state and connection message.
- Make `RemoteConnectButton` open the remote connection dialog when it mounts with a disconnected snapshot containing an error. The existing same-origin connection attempt and manual retry behavior remain responsible for reconnecting and opening the remote project.
- Do not suppress other project restoration errors. They must continue through the existing bootstrap error dialog and Sentry reporting path.
- Add focused tests for recoverable remote startup failure, completion of the remaining startup work, connection-dialog presentation, retry, and continued reporting of unexpected restore failures.

No desktop-host or remote-control protocol change is required.

## Acceptance criteria

- An unavailable remote desktop during last-project restoration does not show `Could not restore last project: Remote-control connection failed`.
- The expected initial remote connection failure is not reported to Sentry.
- Startup completes and the main window becomes available after the connection failure.
- The remote connection dialog shows the connection failure and allows the user to retry.
- A successful retry connects to the remote desktop and opens its active project through the existing flow.
- Startup work after project restoration still runs when the remote connection is unavailable.
- Non-connection project restoration failures retain the existing restore dialog and Sentry reporting behavior.

---

## Current state

The exception is raised in `runPopupAction` when a live agent run is detected but the prompt draft selected for that run is empty. The Sentry stack shows that the path was entered through the prompt editor's `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` shortcut.

The shortcut handler reads part of its run state from the last React render. A scheduled run can become active before React rerenders, so the shortcut can pass validation using stale idle state. `runPopupAction` then reads the current active run, switches to the active conversation draft, and reports `Queued agent prompt is empty`.

The scheduler previously created a replacement conversation for every scheduled run. That defect is already fixed. Schedule registration now stores the displayed `AgentConversation.id`, and scheduled execution validates and continues that conversation with its persisted reference. The desktop and renderer therefore use the same canonical conversation identity.

## Implementation details

- In the prompt shortcut handler, derive the complete run state from a fresh `currentActionRun(bindingStore)` snapshot immediately before dispatch. Do not combine a fresh run with render-captured status or action-type values.
- In `runPopupAction`, treat an empty prompt discovered after an agent run becomes active as a stale UI interaction. Return without creating a submission, enqueueing a prompt, or reporting an error.
- Keep the desktop queue validation that rejects empty prompts. It remains the defensive boundary for invalid bridge calls.
- Do not change scheduler conversation continuation. It already persists `conversationId`, validates the conversation's action and card ownership, and supplies `continueFrom` when the schedule fires.
- Add focused renderer tests for an externally started or scheduled run becoming active before the shortcut handler rerenders.

## Acceptance criteria

- Pressing `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` after a scheduled agent run becomes active but before the prompt UI rerenders does not report `Queued agent prompt is empty`.
- The stale shortcut does not create a submission or call the queued-prompt bridge.
- A non-empty prompt entered for an active agent run is still queued normally.
- Empty queued prompts sent directly to the desktop bridge are still rejected.
- A schedule created for an existing conversation continues the same `AgentConversation.id` and does not create a replacement conversation.
- Scheduled runs without an existing conversation continue to allocate one new conversation identity.

title: deleting a card jumps the scrollbar back to start
status: ready for implementation

policy:
after: 41d340e6-afae-44bd-82e7-41ab673c94e0
---

## Current state

Deleting a card from a long column can move the board scrollbar back to the start. The board and its scroll container are not remounted: card deletion emits granular lifecycle events, `useCardColumnCards` updates only the affected column, and the remaining cards keep stable keys.

The delete confirmation dialog closes before the asynchronous deletion completes. Its automatic focus restoration can target a control owned by the card or card-details popup that is being removed. The deletion flow does not select a stable replacement focus target, so browser focus restoration can move the shared board scroll container.

## Implementation details

- Before deletion, determine the next card in the deleted card's column. Use the previous card when the deleted card is last.
- Disable automatic focus restoration in `CardDeleteDialog` so the dialog does not focus a control that is being removed.
- After the card has been removed from the rendered column, focus the replacement card with `focus({ preventScroll: true })`. Identify the card by `Card.header.internalId`, not by its path.
- If the column has no remaining cards, focus its Add card button with `preventScroll`.
- Apply the same behavior when deletion starts from a board card menu or the card-details popup.
- Keep the existing granular card and column subscriptions. Do not remount the board or add a general snapshot refresh.
- Add focused tests for replacement selection, empty-column fallback, both deletion entry points, and focus with `preventScroll`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deleting a card while scrolled down a long column does not move the board scrollbar back to the start.
- After deletion, focus moves to the next card in the same column without scrolling it. If there is no next card, focus moves to the previous card.
- Deleting the only card in a column moves focus to that column's Add card button without changing the board scroll position beyond the browser's required range.
- Deletion from the board card menu and the card-details popup has the same focus and scroll behavior.
- Cancelling the confirmation dialog retains the existing focus restoration behavior and does not delete the card.
- Only the affected column membership and deleted card are rerendered; the board scroll container remains mounted.

1	import { useCallback, useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react'
2	import { orderByAfter, UNASSIGNED_STATUS } from '../../data/card_ordering'
3	import {
4	    CARD_ADDED_EVENT,
5	    CARD_REMOVED_EVENT,
6	    cardCollectionFieldChangedEvent,
7	    dataService,
8	    type CardAddedEventDetail,
9	    type CardRemovedEventDetail,
10	    type DataService,
11	} from '../../services/data/data_service'
12	
13	function cardStatus(event: Event) {
14	    return (event as CustomEvent<CardAddedEventDetail | CardRemovedEventDetail>).detail.card.header.status
15	        ?? UNASSIGNED_STATUS
16	}
17	
18	function areSamePaths(first: string[], second: string[]) {
19	    return first.length === second.length && second.every((path, index) => first[index] === path)
20	}
21	
22	/** Subscribes to ordered membership changes for one board column, not card data edits. */
23	export function useCardColumnCards(status: string, service: DataService = dataService) {
24	    const pathsRef = useRef<string[]>([])
25	    const subscribe = useCallback((onStoreChange: () => void) => {
26	        const handleCardAddedOrRemoved = (event: Event) => {
27	            if (cardStatus(event) === status) {
28	                onStoreChange()
29	            }
30	        }
31	        service.addEventListener(CARD_ADDED_EVENT, handleCardAddedOrRemoved)
32	        service.addEventListener(cardCollectionFieldChangedEvent('ordering'), onStoreChange)
33	        service.addEventListener(CARD_REMOVED_EVENT, handleCardAddedOrRemoved)
34	
35	        return () => {
36	            service.removeEventListener(CARD_ADDED_EVENT, handleCardAddedOrRemoved)
37	            service.removeEventListener(cardCollectionFieldChangedEvent('ordering'), onStoreChange)
38	            service.removeEventListener(CARD_REMOVED_EVENT, handleCardAddedOrRemoved)
39	        }
40	    }, [service, status])
41	    const getSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
42	        const cards = service.getState().snapshot?.activeCards ?? []
43	        const nextPaths = orderByAfter(cards.filter((card) => (
44	            (card.header.status ?? UNASSIGNED_STATUS) === status
45	        ))).map((card) => card.path)
46	        if (areSamePaths(pathsRef.current, nextPaths)) return pathsRef.current
47	
48	        pathsRef.current = nextPaths
49	
50	        return nextPaths
51	    }, [service, status])
52	
53	    return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getSnapshot)
54	}

entries.content:
## Change plan for B_350 (no edits made yet)

**The problem:** In MUI 9.2, the dialog's focus trap decides whether to restore focus when the dialog opens, not when it closes (`FocusTrap.js:144-155`; the effect only re-runs when `open` changes). So `disableRestoreFocus` can't be switched on just for the Delete path. If I set it permanently, Cancel stops restoring focus, which breaks the acceptance criterion about cancelling. Block 1 works around this.

### Block 1: `card_delete_dialog.tsx`
- Always set `disableRestoreFocus` on the `Dialog`.
- When focus first enters the dialog, store the element it came from (the focus event's `relatedTarget`). MUI uses the same source to pick the element it restores.
- On Cancel, Escape or a backdrop click: close the dialog, then focus the stored element in a microtask (after the dialog has closed, so its focus trap can't pull focus back).
- On Delete: close without restoring focus.
- New test file `card_delete_dialog.test.tsx`:
  - Cancel restores focus to the element that opened the dialog and does not delete the card.
  - Delete does not restore focus.

### Block 2: new `card_deletion_focus.ts`, plus attributes for finding the focus target
- `resolveDeletionFocusTarget(columns, path)` is a pure function. It finds the column that holds the card and returns, in order of preference:
  - the next card's `header.internalId`;
  - otherwise the previous card's `header.internalId`;
  - otherwise the column status, meaning "focus this column's Add card button".
- `focusDeletionTarget(rootElement, target)` looks up the target element inside the board root and calls `focus({ preventScroll: true })`.
- `project_card_drag_container.tsx`: add `data-card-internal-id` to the card's drag button, which is the card's focusable element. This needs a new `cardInternalId` prop.
- `card_column.tsx`: add `data-add-card-status` to the Add card button.
- Unit tests:
  - picks the next card, or the previous one when the deleted card is last;
  - falls back to the Add button when the column becomes empty;
  - focuses with `preventScroll: true`.

### Block 3: `card_view.tsx` `handleDeleteCard`
- Before deleting, work out the focus target from `currentCardColumns(states)`.
- After `deleteCard`, `clearSelectedPath` and `closeCardDetailsByInternalId`, focus that target.
- Both entry points (board card menu and card-details popup) already go through this handler, so one change covers both.
- Column subscriptions stay as they are, and nothing remounts.
- Tests in `card_view.test.tsx`:
  - deleting from the card menu focuses the next card;
  - deleting from the card-details popup does the same;
  - deleting the only card in a column focuses its Add card button;
  - every one of these focus calls uses `preventScroll`.

### Block 4: checks and spec status
- Run lint, typecheck and the related test files only.
- Set `status: ready` in the spec file under `md2`.

### Open points
1. **Mobile board:** `mobile_card_view.tsx` has its own copy of `handleDeleteCard`. The spec only covers the desktop board, so my plan is to leave it out. It will still get the Block 1 change, because that dialog is shared. Do you want mobile to get the replacement focus as well?
2. **Timing:** after `deleteCard` resolves, the deleted card may not have left the DOM yet. That doesn't matter for focus: the replacement card and the Add button are never removed, so I focus right away without waiting for an animation frame.

Waiting for your approval.

entries.content:
Deleting a card on the desktop board now moves focus to a neighbouring card (or the column's Add card button) without scrolling the board. Lint, typecheck and the related test files pass. I haven't checked the scroll behaviour in the running app; the tests confirm focus moves with `preventScroll`, not the scrollbar position. The spec status is now `ready`.

**What changed:**
- **`card_delete_dialog.tsx`:** the dialog no longer lets MUI restore focus. MUI decides that when the dialog opens, so it can't be turned off just for Delete. Instead, the dialog remembers the element that had focus before it opened.
  - On Cancel, Escape or a backdrop click, it puts focus back on that element after closing, so cancelling behaves as before.
  - On Delete, it restores nothing.
- **`card_deletion_focus.ts` (new):**
  - `resolveCardDeletionFocusTarget` runs before the delete and picks the next card in the column, the previous card if the deleted one was last, or the column's Add card button if it was the only card.
  - `focusCardDeletionTarget` finds that element by the card's `internalId` (or the column status) and focuses it with `preventScroll: true`.
- **Markers for finding the target:** each card's drag button now has `data-card-internal-id`, and each Add card button has `data-add-card-status`.
- **`card_view.tsx` `handleDeleteCard`:** picks the target before deleting and focuses it after the card-details popup closes. The card menu and the card-details popup both go through this handler, so they behave the same. Column subscriptions are unchanged and nothing remounts.

**Tests added:**
- `card_delete_dialog.test.tsx`: Cancel restores focus and doesn't delete; Delete doesn't restore focus.
- `card_deletion_focus.test.ts`: next card, previous card, Add button fallback, card not found, and focus with `preventScroll`.
- `card_view.test.tsx`: deleting from the card menu and from the card-details popup focuses the next card; deleting a column's only card focuses its Add card button.

**Things to know:**
- **Columns that disappear when empty:** a column without `alwaysVisible` is removed once its last card is deleted, so its Add card button is gone too. In that case nothing gets focus. The spec's Add-button fallback only works for always-visible columns.
- **Mobile board:** you didn't answer the mobile question, so I left `mobile_card_view.tsx` out. It still gets the dialog change, so after a delete on mobile nothing takes focus. Say if you want the replacement focus there too.
- **Spec file:** while I was working, someone else removed the `after:` line from its frontmatter. I didn't touch that line; I only changed `status`.

## Current state

Deleting a card from a long column can move the board scrollbar back to the start. The board and its scroll container are not remounted: card deletion emits granular lifecycle events, `useCardColumnCards` updates only the affected column, and the remaining cards keep stable keys.

The delete confirmation dialog closes before the asynchronous deletion completes. Its automatic focus restoration can target a control owned by the card or card-details popup that is being removed. The deletion flow does not select a stable replacement focus target, so browser focus restoration can move the shared board scroll container.

## Implementation details

- Before deletion, determine the next card in the deleted card's column. Use the previous card when the deleted card is last.
- Disable automatic focus restoration in `CardDeleteDialog` so the dialog does not focus a control that is being removed.
- After the card has been removed from the rendered column, focus the replacement card with `focus({ preventScroll: true })`. Identify the card by `Card.header.internalId`, not by its path.
- If the column has no remaining cards, focus its Add card button with `preventScroll`.
- Apply the same behavior when deletion starts from a board card menu or the card-details popup.
- Keep the existing granular card and column subscriptions. Do not remount the board or add a general snapshot refresh.
- Add focused tests for replacement selection, empty-column fallback, both deletion entry points, and focus with `preventScroll`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deleting a card while scrolled down a long column does not move the board scrollbar back to the start.
- After deletion, focus moves to the next card in the same column without scrolling it. If there is no next card, focus moves to the previous card.
- Deleting the only card in a column moves focus to that column's Add card button without changing the board scroll position beyond the browser's required range.
- Deletion from the board card menu and the card-details popup has the same focus and scroll behavior.
- Cancelling the confirmation dialog retains the existing focus restoration behavior and does not delete the card.
- Only the affected column membership and deleted card are rerendered; the board scroll container remains mounted.

readonly agents: AgentIntegration
    readonly cards: CardOperations
    readonly conversationPins: ConversationPinService
    readonly projectLoading: ProjectLoading
    readonly releases: ReleaseOperations

    private commitBatcher: CommitBatcher | null = null
    private remarkableBridge: RemarkableBridge | null = null
    private storage: StorageService | null = null
    private fullProjectLoaded = false
    private readonly reportedAgentReferenceMigrationConflicts: Set<string> = new Set()
    private readonly projectState: ProjectState
    private readonly saveStateService: SaveStateService
    private persistenceSnapshot: DataPersistenceSnapshot = { hasPendingFileCommit: false, hasPendingPush: false, isSaving: false }

    constructor() {
        super()
        this.saveStateService = new SaveStateService()
        this.saveStateService.addEventListener('changed', () => this.dispatchPersistenceChanged())
        this.projectState = new ProjectState(
            (card) => this.agents.attachCardAgentConversations(card),
            (previousCards, nextCards) => this.dispatchCardChanges(previousCards, nextCards),
            reportCardParseErrors,
        )
        this.conversationPins = new ConversationPinService({
            getPinnedConversations: () => configService.isInitialized()
                ? configService.getProjectConfig().pinnedConversations
                : [],
            saveConversationPinned: (locator, pinned) => configService.setConversationPinned(locator, pinned),
            subscribeConfig: (listener) => {
                configService.addEventListener('changed', listener)

                return () => configService.removeEventListener('changed', listener)
            },
        })
        this.cards = new CardOperations(
            this.createCardOperationsDependencies(),
            (cardPath, state) => this.agents.triggerStateActions(cardPath, state),
        )
        this.agents = new AgentIntegration(this.createAgentIntegrationDependencies())
        agentAcknowledgementService.connectConversationStore((conversation) => this.agents.findStoredConversation(conversation))

export function cardFieldChangedEvent(path: string, field: CardField) {

}

/** Event name for collection projections affected by one field across cards. */
export function cardCollectionFieldChangedEvent(field: CardField) {
    return `${CARD_CHANGED_EVENT}:all:${field}`
}

entries.content:
The original diagnosis was incomplete. The scrollbar movement is caused by browser scroll anchoring, not focus restoration.

Evidence from [delete card.json](<C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/delete card.json>):

- At `+22 ms`, the affected `CardColumn` updates.
- At `+232 ms`, Chrome records `ScrollLayer` with `NotifyScroll type: "anchoring"` on the board’s scrolling `MuiBox`.
- At `+337 ms`, the actual `scroll` event occurs.
- Replacement focus does not occur until `+1.502 s`.

Therefore, `focus({ preventScroll: true })` runs too late to prevent the jump. The board’s vertical scroll container is [card_view.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/card_view/card_view.tsx:254), and deleting a card changes its layout, allowing Chrome’s scroll-anchor algorithm to adjust it.

There is also genuine broad refresh-like work:

- Deletion rebuilds the project snapshot through [project_state.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_state.ts:280).
- It then emits the broad `changed` event in [project_file_operations.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/data/project_file_operations.ts:110).
- The trace consequently shows unrelated toolbar and file-tree rendering.

However, the board root itself is not remounted. The trace shows the affected column updating, the deleted card unmounting, and later its follower updating; it does not show a full `CardView` remount.

The immediate scrollbar fix should be disabling scroll anchoring on the board scroll container with `overflowAnchor: 'none'`. The existing `preventScroll` focus handling should remain. The broad `changed` event is a separate performance concern requiring a granular project-file/repository notification instead of a general snapshot publication.

No files were changed.
ok, fix it

I’ll apply the narrow scroll-anchoring fix to the existing board scroll container, then run the focused card-view tests and lint. I’ll leave the broader project-state refresh path unchanged because it is a separate behavioral change.

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.
